Hi Sven,

Thanks — good questions. I'll summarize the answers below and loop in our privacy and ops leads for detail and artifacts. High level:

- EU-only processing: Redwood supports in-region inference and data residency. For Delacorp we propose an EU-only processing configuration (we call it "EU-exclusive"), where customer compute, storage, and encryption keys are pinned to EU regions (Frankfurt and Amsterdam). The control plane remains logically global but we can scope certain operator actions to EU-only and require customer approval for out-of-region intervention.

- Regional failover: automated failover within EU availability zones is default. Cross-border failover outside the EU is not enabled for EU-exclusive customers except under an explicit, pre-approved emergency playbook. In such a rare emergency, we fall back to an agreed secondary EU region first; only if all EU capacity/liveliness is compromised would we consider out-of-EU fallback, and that requires three approvals (customer emergency contact, Redwood security lead, and regional ops manager) and is fully logged.

Soojin & Naomi — can you confirm the following items from the checklist and share the artifacts Sven requested? Specifically:

- Confirmation of operator access controls, and a sample operator-access audit log extract (redacted).
- Proof that KMS keys for Delacorp are created in EU and never exported (KMS key matrix).
- Architecture diagram showing failover behavior (regional-failover-diagram.png).
- Statement we can add to the DPA/SCCs about the emergency approval process.

I'll collect and upload to the shared Drive link and respond before COB next Friday.

Cheers,
Rishi

Subject: Operator access, KMS, and technical controls (details)

Hi all,

Following Rishi's note — below are concise answers and pointers to where we'll upload artifacts. I'll add Andreas for a privacy consultancy review.

1) Operator access:
- Operators (Redwood SRE and on-call engineers) are role-separated. Elevated access requires an internal ticket and is time-limited.
- We maintain immutable audit logs of sudo/session activity; redacted extracts will be provided showing access to the customer environment with timestamps and justification.

2) KMS and key locality:
- We provision customer-specific AES-256 CMKs in the customer's selected EU region via our KMS. Keys are never exported and are region-bound. The KMS key matrix (attached) maps customer -> key id -> region -> created_at.

3) Failover logic:
- Primary: in-region within same AZ cluster (no cross-region).
- Secondary (EU-only): automated cross-AZ/cross-region within EU (Frankfurt <-> Amsterdam).
- Tertiary (out-of-EU): cold failover only, requires the three-party approval described by Rishi; before enabling we pseudonymize active payloads and rotate ephemeral session keys; full audit trail is produced.

4) Data deletion: standard retention lifecycle (S3 lifecycle + internal purge jobs). We can provide a sample deletion certificate and bucket lifecycle configuration.

I'll upload: regional-failover-diagram.png, kms-key-matrix.csv, operator-audit-sample.txt, deletion-certificate.pdf to the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin
